newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares firm on rally hopes, end of year.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares firm on rally hopes, end of year.

text.p: A scarcity of paper available to investors anticipating a New Year's rally and a move by some brokers to hike prices to show good end-of-year results lifted Russian share prices in thin trading on Friday, dealers said.

One dealer said utility UES traded up to 9 U.S. cents, though Reuters data showed it trading at $0.0877 on the over the counter market after finishing at $0.0864 on Thursday. LUKoil rose to $11.20 from $10.80.
Dealers said some local banks were raising prices to bolster end of year results but this would stop in the new year.
Shares will trade on Monday and Tuesday, but the market will then close for four days of holidays, reopening on Sunday January 5.
"We won't see a single bid on the fifth," said Alexei Abdurakhimov, chief trader of MFK-Moscow Partners.
Volumes on the Russian Trading System appeared higher than on Thursday, near $3-$4 million, and a number of shares gained 3-5 percent.
Troika Dialog's Terry Olin said stock was changing hands on the offer side.
"I imagine UES is up on a leak of information as to the outcome of the auction or speculation that the block has been bought at a minimum of 9 cents," he said.
The government has auctioned 8.5 percent of UES, for which bids were accepted up to December 23.

Traders said some investors were eager to get invested in the market before a January rally but were frustrated by a lack of available stock since many market partcipants were not working over the Christmas and New Year holidays.

Dealers who said the Friday rally was based on real demand and those who said there was an artificial end-of-year push said there would likely be a correction at the beginning of the year before prices began rising again.
"People will come back to work and take a look at their portfolios, see prices have moved dramatically higher and take some profits," said Olin.
"But I don't think that (correction) will last long."
